name: Relative Strength Index
description: Measures the speed and magnitude of recent price changes to identify overbought or oversold conditions. Developed by J. Welles Wilder. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}
formula: RSI = 100 – [100 ÷ (1 + RS)] where RS = Average Gain over N periods ÷ Average Loss over N periods. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
parameters: Typical period N = 14; adjustable depending on timeframe.

signal.buy: RSI crosses above ~30 (or adjusted lower threshold) from below signaling potential rebound
signal.sell: RSI crosses below ~70 (or adjusted upper threshold) from above signaling potential pull-back
signal.neutral: RSI between ~30 and ~70 indicates neither extreme condition

best_timeframe: Short to medium-term (e.g., 1-hour to daily charts); adaptable depending on setting
strengths: Simple to interpret; widely recognised; good at highlighting overbought/oversold and divergences
weaknesses: Can stay in overbought/oversold zones for extended time in strong trends; gives false signals in choppy market

name: Stochastic Oscillator
description: Compares the current closing price of a security to its price range over a specified period to gauge momentum and potential turning points. Developed by George Lane. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
formula: %K = (Current Close – Lowest Low in n periods) ÷ (Highest High in n periods – Lowest Low in n periods) × 100; %D = SMA of %K (commonly 3-period) :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}
parameters: Typical look-back period n = 14 for %K; %D often 3-period SMA of %K.

signal.buy: %K crosses above %D in oversold region (e.g., below ~20) signalling upward momentum likely
signal.sell: %K crosses below %D in overbought region (e.g., above ~80) signalling downward momentum likely
signal.neutral: The %K and %D lines staying between ~20-80 without clear cross or trend indicates no strong signal

best_timeframe: Short timeframes (e.g., intraday 15-min to 1-hour) but also usable on daily charts depending on setting
strengths: Responsive to recent price changes; helps identify momentum shifts and turning points; useful in range-bound markets
weaknesses: Can give many false signals in strong trending markets; may require adjustment of thresholds; smoothing may reduce responsiveness

name: Simple Moving Average
description: A simple arithmetic moving average that smooths price data by calculating the average of recent closing prices over a specified number of periods. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}
formula: SMA(n) = (P₁ + P₂ + … + Pₙ) ÷ n, where P = closing price and n = number of periods. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
parameters: Typical period n = 20, 50, 200 depending on timeframe.

signal.buy: Price crosses above the SMA line (or short‐term SMA crosses above long‐term SMA) signalling upward trend
signal.sell: Price crosses below the SMA line (or short‐term SMA crosses below long‐term SMA) signalling downward trend
signal.neutral: Price remains close to the SMA with no clear directional crossover

best_timeframe: Medium to long-term (e.g., daily, weekly) but can be used intraday with shorter lengths.
strengths: Simple to calculate and interpret; smooths out noise; good for identifying trend direction and support/resistance levels.
weaknesses: Lags the price because it gives equal weight to all periods; less responsive in fast changing markets; crossovers may produce false signals in choppy or range‐bound conditions. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

name: Exponential Moving Average
description: An exponential moving average that gives greater weight to more recent prices, thereby reacting faster to price changes than the simple moving average. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
formula: EMA_today = (Price_today × multiplier) + (EMA_yesterday × (1 − multiplier)); where Multiplier = 2 ÷ (n + 1) for period n. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
parameters: Typical period n = 12, 26, 50 depending on timeframe and strategy.

signal.buy: Price crosses above the EMA line (or short‐period EMA crosses above longer‐period EMA) signalling bullish momentum
signal.sell: Price crosses below the EMA line (or short‐period EMA crosses below longer‐period EMA) signalling bearish momentum
signal.neutral: Price oscillates around the EMA without a clear directional crossover

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (e.g., intraday to daily) due to faster responsiveness.
strengths: More responsive to recent price changes than SMA; good for catching early trend shifts; widely used in cross-MA strategies.
weaknesses: Still lags to some extent; more prone to false signals in sideways or highly volatile markets; needs parameter adjustment for different assets/timeframes. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}

name: Moving Average Convergence Divergence
description: A momentum and trend-following indicator that shows the relationship between two exponential moving averages of price, and includes a signal line and histogram. Developed by Gerald Appel. :contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}
formula: MACD line = EMA₁₂ − EMA₂₆; Signal line = EMA₉ of MACD line; Histogram = MACD line − Signal line. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}
parameters: Typical settings: 12-period EMA, 26-period EMA, 9-period signal line.

signal.buy: MACD line crosses above the signal line (histogram turns positive) signalling bullish momentum
signal.sell: MACD line crosses below the signal line (histogram turns negative) signalling bearish momentum
signal.neutral: MACD and signal line close together and histogram near zero indicating no strong momentum

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (e.g., 1-hour to daily charts) but can also be used for swing trades.
strengths: Captures momentum shifts and trend reversals; combines trend and momentum in one indicator; widely used and recognized.
weaknesses: Lagging by its nature (since based on EMAs); may give false signals in range-bound markets; histogram can confuse less experienced traders. :contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}

name: Bollinger Bands®
description: A volatility-based band indicator created by John Bollinger that plots a moving average and upper & lower bands at a multiple of standard deviations away, giving a dynamically adjusting envelope around price. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}
formula: Middle Band = SMA(n); Upper Band = SMA(n) + (K × σ_n); Lower Band = SMA(n) − (K × σ_n), where σ_n is the standard deviation of price over n periods. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
parameters: Typical settings: n = 20 periods for the SMA, K = 2 standard deviations. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}

signal.buy: Price touches or closes below the Lower Band and then starts moving back up (in expectation of reversion or breakout).
signal.sell: Price touches or closes above the Upper Band and then starts moving down (in expectation of reversion) or breaks out upward with strong momentum.
signal.neutral: Price remains between bands without meaningful band-width change or breakout; bands are relatively stable.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) where volatility changes are meaningful; works across timeframes but settings may adapt. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
strengths: Adapts to changing volatility; gives clear visual envelope; can highlight overbought/oversold extremes relative to range.
weaknesses: Being reactive, it does not predict direction; in strong trending markets price can ride the band (upper or lower) giving misleading “overbought/oversold” cues; requires confirmation from other tools. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}

name: Stochastic Oscillator
description: A momentum indicator developed by George Lane that compares a closing price to its recent high-low range in order to gauge momentum and potential reversal points. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}
formula: %K = (Close − LowestLow_N) ÷ (HighestHigh_N − LowestLow_N) × 100; %D = SMA3(%K) or a moving average of %K. :contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}
parameters: Typical setting: N = 14 periods for look-back; %D smoothing often 3 periods. :contentReference[oaicite:11]{index=11}

signal.buy: %K crosses above %D in oversold zone (e.g., below ~20) or divergence where price makes new low but oscillator does not.
signal.sell: %K crosses below %D in overbought zone (e.g., above ~80) or divergence where price makes new high but oscillator does not.
signal.neutral: %K and %D move without crossing or are between ~20-80 without clear momentum shift.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) especially suited for range or reversal setups.
strengths: Responsive to momentum shifts; gives early signals of potential turning points; good for range-bound and oscillating markets.
weaknesses: Can give many false signals in strong trends (where momentum stays high); must be used with trend context; thresholds may need adjustment. :contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}

name: Average True Range
description: A volatility indicator developed by J. Welles Wilder that measures the average range of price movements (including gaps) over a specified period. :contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}
formula: TR_t = max[(High_t − Low_t), |High_t − Close_{t−1}|, |Low_t − Close_{t−1}|]; ATR_initial = (1/n) × ∑_{i=1}^n TR_i; ATR_t = ( (ATR_{t−1} × (n-1)) + TR_t ) / n. :contentReference[oaicite:15]{index=15}
parameters: Typical setting: n = 14 periods; can use shorter/longer periods depending on timeframe. :contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}

signal.buy: Rising ATR suggests increasing volatility which can support a breakout trade; entry triggered when breakout occurs above a range plus ATR multiple.
signal.sell: Also rising ATR can indicate strong move in either direction; for risk management, high ATR may prompt widening of stops or reduction of position size.
signal.neutral: Stable or low ATR suggests range or consolidation—less ideal for breakout trades, wait for volatility expansion.

best_timeframe: Any timeframe (intraday, daily, weekly) for measuring volatility; especially useful for setting stops/exits and breakout timing.
strengths: Non-directional but highly useful for volatility measurement, stop-loss sizing, breakout assessment; adapts to different assets/timeframes.
weaknesses: Does not give direction or trend; cannot be used alone for buy/sell direction; high value does not guarantee favourable move direction. :contentReference[oaicite:17]{index=17}

name: Commodity Channel Index
description: An oscillator developed by Donald Lambert that measures the current price level relative to the average price level over a specified period. Used to identify overbought/oversold conditions and early trend shifts. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
formula: CCI = (Typical Price – SMA(Typical Price, n)) ÷ (0.015 × Mean Deviation), where Typical Price = (High + Low + Close) ÷ 3. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
parameters: Typical period n = 20 (or sometimes 14); constant = 0.015. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

signal.buy: CCI crosses above -100 (or moves from below toward +100) signalling potential upward rebound or new up-trend
signal.sell: CCI crosses below +100 (or moves from above toward -100) signalling potential downward reversal or new down-trend
signal.neutral: CCI remains between –100 and +100 with no clear breakout of extremes; indicates no strong deviation yet

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (daily or shorter) though oscillatory behaviour means works well in both intra-day and swing contexts. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
strengths: Can identify early trend shifts and over-extensions; more flexible than bounded oscillators because not capped; good for spotting divergences and cycle extremes.
weaknesses: Unbounded and setting levels are subjective; may give false signals in very volatile or choppy markets; lag appears because based on moving averages. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}

name: Average Directional Index
description: An indicator developed by J. Welles Wilder Jr. that measures the strength of a trend (regardless of direction) using the Directional Movement system (+DI, -DI). :contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}
formula: ADX is derived from +DI and -DI: first calculate True Range (TR), +DM, -DM, then smoothed +DI = (Smoothed +DM / Smoothed TR) ×100, same for -DI; DX = |+DI - -DI| / (+DI + -DI) ×100; ADX = smoothed average of DX (typically 14-period). :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}
parameters: Typical period = 14; thresholds often: ADX >25 or >40 to indicate strong trend. :contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}

signal.buy: Trend strength rising (ADX crosses upward above ~25) while +DI > -DI signals a strong bullish trend
signal.sell: Trend strength rising while -DI > +DI signals a strong bearish trend
signal.neutral: ADX below ~20-25 indicates weak or no trend (range-bound) — best to avoid trending strategies

best_timeframe: Medium term (4-hour to daily) but can be used for shorter timeframes if adapted; best when confirming trend presence rather than timing entries.
strengths: Helps distinguish trending vs ranging markets; useful filter for other indicators; less direction-biased, focuses on strength only.
weaknesses: Lagging by nature (since smoothing required); does not show direction by itself; may give delayed signals in fast-moving markets. :contentReference[oaicite:11]{index=11}

name: On-Balance Volume
description: A cumulative volume-based indicator popularised by Joe Granville which adds or subtracts volume depending on whether the closing price rose or fell, used to confirm price trends or spot divergences. :contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}
formula: If Close_t > Close_{t-1} then OBV_t = OBV_{t-1} + Volume_t; if Close_t < Close_{t-1} then OBV_t = OBV_{t-1} − Volume_t; if equal then OBV_t = OBV_{t-1}. :contentReference[oaicite:15]{index=15}
parameters: No built-in smoothing required; starting value can be zero or prior known value; timeframe same as price series.

signal.buy: OBV rises while price also rising (confirming trend) or OBV divergence (price falling while OBV rising) signals potential reversal
signal.sell: OBV falls while price also falling (confirming downtrend) or OBV divergence (price rising while OBV flat or falling) signals potential weakness
signal.neutral: OBV moves flat or mirrors price without showing divergence or strong volume flow — uncertain confirmation

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) for confirming volume flow; can be used across timeframes.
strengths: Simple to calculate and interpret; volume-aware confirmation of price moves; good for spotting divergence between price and volume.
weaknesses: Does not directly give entry/exit signals; cumulative nature means starting point affects absolute values; less useful in low-volume or illiquid markets. :contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}

name: Fibonacci Retracement Levels
description: A tool that identifies potential support and resistance levels by plotting horizontal lines at key Fibonacci ratios after a significant price move. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}
formula: Select two extreme points (High and Low). Then calculate levels: Low + (High-Low) × 23.6 %, 38.2 %, 50 %, 61.8 %. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
parameters: Swing high & swing low points; typical retracement levels: 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8% (optionally 78.6%). :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}

signal.buy: Price retraces to a Fibonacci level (e.g., 38.2 % or 61.8 %) and shows bullish reversal price action from that level.
signal.sell: Price retraces to a Fibonacci level and shows bearish reversal price action (e.g., in a down-trend, retrace to 61.8 % then resume down).
signal.neutral: Price is between levels without clear reaction or reversal; no strong signal.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) — useful for pullbacks and entries in trending markets.
strengths: Helps identify logical entry zones on pullbacks; aligns with support/resistance levels; widely used and therefore self-fulfilling to some degree.
weaknesses: Highly subjective (choice of swing points); levels often broken in strong momentum moves; not a signal generator by itself (needs confirmation). :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

name: Aroon Oscillator
description: An indicator derived from the Aroon Indicator which measures how many periods have passed since the highest high / lowest low and signals the strength and change of trends. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
formula: Aroon Up = [(n − periods since highest high in last n) ÷ n] ×100; Aroon Down = [(n − periods since lowest low in last n) ÷ n] ×100; Aroon Oscillator = Aroon Up - Aroon Down. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}
parameters: Typical period n = 14 or 25; oscillator range -100 to +100. :contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}

signal.buy: Aroon Oscillator crosses above zero (i.e., Aroon Up > Aroon Down) signalling an emerging uptrend.
signal.sell: Aroon Oscillator crosses below zero (Aroon Down > Aroon Up) signalling an emerging downtrend.
signal.neutral: Aroon Oscillator is around zero and neither uptrend nor downtrend is clearly dominating.

best_timeframe: Medium term (4-hour to daily) but can be adapted to shorter timeframes with care.
strengths: Good at identifying start of new trends and distinguishing trending vs range markets; simple to interpret as a single line. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}
weaknesses: Does not show magnitude of trend, only time-based; in volatile/choppy markets it may give false signals; needs adaptation to asset behaviour. :contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}

name: Volume Price Trend Indicator
description: An indicator developed by Buff Dormeier that relates price changes to volume by cumulatively adjusting a line based on percentage price change times volume, helping confirm trend strength and volume flow. :contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}
formula: VPT_t = VPT_{t-1} + Volume_t × [(Close_t – Close_{t-1}) ÷ Close_{t-1}]. :contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}
parameters: Start value arbitrary (often zero); uses daily (or chosen timeframe) volume and closing prices.

signal.buy: VPT trending upward (higher highs) in line with price uptrend — confirming buying pressure.
signal.sell: VPT trending downward (lower highs) while price uptrend or showing divergence (price up, VPT down) — warning of weakness.
signal.neutral: VPT flat or moving with price without clear divergence or momentum change.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) for confirming price-volume relationships.
strengths: Combines price and volume for trend confirmation; useful for spotting divergences and validating moves. :contentReference[oaicite:15]{index=15}
weaknesses: Does not give primary entry/exit timing; cumulative nature means absolute values are arbitrary; less effective in very low volume or illiquid markets. :contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}

name: Williams Percent Range
description: A momentum indicator developed by Larry Williams that shows the current closing price relative to the high-low range over a specified look-back period, helping identify overbought and oversold conditions. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
formula: %R = (Highest High_n − Close_today) ÷ (Highest High_n − Lowest Low_n) × (−100) where n is look-back period (commonly 14). :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
parameters: Typical look-back period n = 14; scale is 0 to −100. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}

signal.buy: %R rises above the oversold threshold (e.g., crosses above -80) or divergence where price makes a new low but %R does not.
signal.sell: %R falls below the overbought threshold (e.g., crosses below -20) or divergence where price makes new high but %R does not.
signal.neutral: %R is between typical thresholds (e.g., -80 to -20) and provides no strong signal.

best_timeframe: Short-term (intraday to daily) due to its sensitivity; effective in swing and range-bound markets.
strengths: Very responsive to recent price changes; good for identifying overbought/oversold extremes and divergences. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
weaknesses: Can generate false signals in strong trending markets (where overbought/oversold zones can persist); does not indicate trend strength. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}

name: Moving Average Envelopes / Channels
description: An indicator which plots lines (envelopes) above and below a moving average (simple or exponential) at a fixed percentage distance, helping identify trend direction and over-extension from the mean. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
formula: Center line = MA(n); Upper envelope = MA(n) × (1 + p); Lower envelope = MA(n) × (1 − p) where p is the percentage deviation. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}
parameters: Typical MA period n = 20; envelope deviation percentage p = 2-5% or chosen based on asset volatility. :contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}

signal.buy: Price breaks above upper envelope indicating strong trend/momentum, or price pulls back to envelope and rebounds upward.
signal.sell: Price breaks below lower envelope indicating strong downward trend/momentum, or price rallies to upper envelope and stalls/reverses.
signal.neutral: Price remains within the envelopes and no breakout or clear bounce off envelope is visible.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) especially useful for trending or mean-reversion setups depending on strategy.
strengths: Helps visualise deviation from average; good for identifying extended moves or pullbacks; customizable for asset volatility. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}
weaknesses: Choice of percentage is subjective; in strong trends price may ride envelope giving misleading over-extension signals; lag inherent in MA. :contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}

name: True Strength Index
description: A momentum indicator developed by William Blau that uses double-smoothed price changes (and absolute price changes) to reduce noise, assess momentum, trend direction and possible reversals. :contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}
formula: TSI = 100 × (Double-Smoothed PriceChange ÷ Double-Smoothed Absolute PriceChange). For example, first compute PC = Close_t − Close_{t-1}, then EMA_r of PC, then EMA_s of that result, likewise absolute PC. :contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}
parameters: Typical smoothing parameters: r = 25, s = 13 for the double EMA smoothing; signal line often 7- to 12-period EMA of TSI. :contentReference[oaicite:14]{index=14}

signal.buy: TSI crosses above signal line (or crosses above zero) indicating strength; divergence where price falls but TSI rises.
signal.sell: TSI crosses below signal line (or crosses below zero) indicating weakness; divergence where price rises but TSI falls.
signal.neutral: TSI oscillates near zero or signal line without clear cross or trend direction.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) suitable for capturing momentum shifts and trend changes.
strengths: Smoother and less noisy than many oscillators; combines momentum and trend direction; adaptable to multiple timeframes. :contentReference[oaicite:15]{index=15}
weaknesses: Still lagging due to smoothing; signals may be delayed in fast moves; divergence and crossovers sometimes generate false positives. :contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}

name: Multi-Timeframe Trend / Volatility Overlay
description: An overlay combining multiple indicators/timeframes (e.g., moving averages across timeframes + volatility measures) to identify alignment of major trend + pullback zones + entry timing. For example: trend direction on daily, pullback zone on 4-hour, entry on 1-hour with volatility filter. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}
formula: No single formula — conceptually: TrendSignal = MA_fast_n1 on timeframe T1 crosses MA_slow_n2; VolatilityFilter = ATR_n3 on T2 > threshold; EntryTrigger = price breaks layer or touches pullback zone on T3. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
parameters: Typical: T1 = Daily (MA periods e.g., 50 & 200), T2 = 4-hour (ATR period 14), T3 = 1-hour (entry timeframe); thresholds & look-backs set per asset.

signal.buy: Trend alignment across higher timeframe (e.g., Daily MA bullish) + volatility expanding on medium timeframe + price pullback or breakout on lower timeframe.
signal.sell: Trend alignment bearish on higher timeframe + medium timeframe volatility expansion + price pullback or lower timeframe breakout to downside.
signal.neutral: Lack of alignment across timeframes or volatility low (range market) → avoid entries or wait.

best_timeframe: Combination of timeframes: higher (daily/weekly) for trend, medium (4H) for pullback/volatility, lower (1H or less) for entry.
strengths: Helps filter trades by ensuring trend, volatility and entry timing align; adds multi-timeframe confluence; reduces trading against higher timeframe trend.
weaknesses: More complex; requires managing/time synchronizing multiple timeframes; may delay signal; more prone to ‘analysis paralysis’; not a plug-and-play simple indicator.

name: Positioning / Flow Indicators (Futures Open Interest / COT)
description: Indicators that analyze futures open interest, the Commitments of Traders Report (COT) data, and other derivatives positioning to gauge how institutional/trader flows may influence price. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
formula: Example: Net_Spec_Long = Speculator_Long − Speculator_Short; COT_Index = (Net_Position − Min(Net_Position, lookback)) ÷ (Max(Net_Position, lookback) − Min(Net_Position, lookback)) ×100. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
parameters: Look-back period often 252 weeks (≈5 years) for normalisation; data categories: Commercials, Large Speculators, Small Traders.

signal.buy: When speculator net positions are extremely short (or commercials very long) relative to historical range → contrarian buy signal.
signal.sell: When speculator net positions are extremely long (or commercials very short) relative to historical range → contrarian sell signal.
signal.neutral: Positioning is near middle of historical range → no strong crowd extreme signal.

best_timeframe: Medium to longer term (weekly data) rather than intraday; usable for swing/position trades rather than exact entry timing.
strengths: Gives insight into what large players are doing; helps detect crowding and potential reversal zones; useful for commodities and futures markets.
weaknesses: Low frequency (often weekly); data lag; does not provide exact entry/exit timing; requires additional technical confirmation.

name: Ichimoku Cloud (Ichimoku Kinko Hyo)
description: A comprehensive indicator developed by Goichi Hosoda in the 1930s / 1960s that provides trend direction, momentum, and future support & resistance levels via its five components: Tenkan-sen, Kijun-sen, Senkou Span A, Senkou Span B, Chikou Span. :contentReference[oaicite:8]{index=8}
formula: Tenkan-sen = (Highest high_n + Lowest low_n) ÷2 for n=9; Kijun-sen = (Highest high_m + Lowest low_m) ÷2 for m=26; Senkou Span A = (Tenkan-sen + Kijun-sen) ÷2 shifted forward 26; Senkou Span B = (Highest high_p + Lowest low_p) ÷2 for p=52 shifted forward 26; Chikou Span = Close shifted back 26. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}
parameters: Typical default: 9,26,52 periods; settings can be adjusted for scalping or swing (e.g., 6,13,26 for faster). :contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}

signal.buy: Price above cloud, cloud bullish (Span A above Span B), Tenkan-sen above Kijun-sen; lagging span above price → bullish trend.
signal.sell: Price below cloud, cloud bearish (Span B above Span A), Tenkan-sen below Kijun-sen; lagging span below price → bearish trend.
signal.neutral: Price inside cloud (trend unclear) or cloud flat/thin → market maybe consolidating.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) depending on settings; highly effective in trending markets. :contentReference[oaicite:11]{index=11}
strengths: All-in-one: trend, momentum, support/resistance; forward projection of cloud helps anticipate future zones; works across markets/timeframes.
weaknesses: Relatively complex to interpret; cloud can lag in fast markets; less effective in sideways/range markets; may require parameter tuning. :contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}

name: Supertrend Indicator
description: A trend-following overlay developed by Olivier Seban in 2009 that uses the Average True Range (ATR) and a multiplier to plot a dynamic line above or below price, signalling bullish or bearish trend biases. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
parameters: Typical settings: ATR period = 7-14; Multiplier = 2-4. Defaults often ATR = 10, Multiplier = 3. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}

signal.buy: Price closes above the Supertrend line (line turns underneath price) → bullish trend signal
signal.sell: Price closes below the Supertrend line (line moves above price) → bearish trend signal
signal.neutral: Price and Supertrend line are close, frequent flips occur (ranging market) → no clear trend bias

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) – works best in trending markets rather than sideways. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
strengths: Simple visual trend indicator; adjusts for volatility via ATR; provides dynamic stop-loss/trail level; works across asset classes. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
weaknesses: May lag in fast breakouts; prone to whipsaws in range-bound markets; parameter settings sensitive to asset/timeframe. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}

name: Guppy Multiple Moving Average
description: Developed by Daryl Guppy, GMMA uses two groups of exponential moving averages (short-term & long-term) to gauge trader vs investor attitude and potential breakout or trend reversals. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
formula: Short-term group: EMA (3,5,8,10,12,15); Long-term group: EMA (30,35,40,45,50,60). Evaluate divergence/convergence between groups. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
parameters: Typical short-term EMAs: 3,5,8,10,12,15; long-term EMAs: 30,35,40,45,50,60; timeframe depends on strategy.

signal.buy: Short-term group diverges and rises above long-term group, indicating trend building.
signal.sell: Short-term group converges or falls below long-term group, indicating trend weakening or reversal.
signal.neutral: Groups are intertwined or converging, suggesting consolidation/no clear trend.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) but can also be used for longer term trend analysis.
strengths: Helps identify when traders (short-term EMAs) and investors (long-term EMAs) align; visual representation of changing market psychology.
weaknesses: Complex with many lines; lag inherent in MA; false signals in choppy/sideways markets.

name: DeMarker Indicator (DeM)
description: Developed by Tom DeMark, the DeMarker indicator compares current period high/low to previous period high/low to measure demand and potential exhaustion of move. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
formula: For each period: if High_t > High_{t-1}, Dem_High = High_t − High_{t-1} else Dem_High = 0; similarly for lows. Then DeM = SMA(Dem_High, n) ÷ (SMA(Dem_High, n) + SMA(Dem_Low, n)). Typically n = 14.
parameters: Typical period n = 14; overbought ~0.70-0.75; oversold ~0.30-0.25.

signal.buy: Indicator falls into oversold region (below ~0.25) and then rises above that threshold signalling potential rebound.
signal.sell: Indicator rises into overbought region (above ~0.75) and then falls below that threshold signalling potential reversal.
signal.neutral: Indicator is between ~0.30-0.70 with no clear extremity or reversal signal.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) particularly useful for detecting exhaustion and reversal points.
strengths: Potentially more sensitive to highs/lows than some oscillators; good for reversal timing when used with other tools.
weaknesses: Less known so less widely discussed; thresholds subjective; in strong trending markets can give many false signals.

name: Fractal Indicator
description: Developed by Bill Williams, the Fractal indicator identifies recurring price patterns (five-bar patterns) signalling potential reversal or breakout points. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
formula: Bullish fractal: Low_(t-2) > Low_(t) < Low_(t-1) < Low_(t) < Low_(t+1) < Low_(t+2); Bearish fractal similarly for highs. No numeric smoothing as such—pattern recognition.
parameters: Typically uses 5-bar pattern period; apply across multiple timeframes for confirmation.

signal.buy: Bullish fractal forms (middle bar lowest of five) and is confirmed by price breaking above middle bar high.
signal.sell: Bearish fractal forms (middle bar highest of five) and is confirmed by price breaking below middle bar low.
signal.neutral: Pattern has not clearly formed or broken out; no valid fractal signal yet.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) especially in conjunction with broader trend filter.
strengths: Clear pattern-based signals; often used as triggers with support/resistance; simple rule structure.
weaknesses: Many false signals in range/volatile markets; requires waiting for price confirmation; pattern very short term and may be noise.

name: Keltner Channel
description: A volatility-based channel indicator using an exponential moving average and the Average True Range (ATR) to set bands above and below. Similar to Bollinger Bands but uses ATR for width. :contentReference[oaicite:7]{index=7}
formula: Middle line = EMA(n); Upper band = EMA(n) + (Multiplier × ATR(n)); Lower band = EMA(n) − (Multiplier × ATR(n)). Typical n = 20, multiplier = 1.5-2.
parameters: Typical EMA period = 20; ATR period = 10 or 14; multiplier = 1.5-2.0.

signal.buy: Price breaks above upper band with expansion in volatility and upward momentum.
signal.sell: Price breaks below lower band with downward momentum and volatility increase.
signal.neutral: Price remains between bands with little volatility expansion; no breakout signal.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) for breakout & trend detection.
strengths: Volatility-sensitive; channels adjust for range/expansion; good for breakout and trend capture.
weaknesses: Still lagging due to EMA; bands may get widened in volatile periods leading to fewer signals; false breakouts possible.

name: Parabolic Stop and Reverse (SAR)
description: Developed by Welles Wilder, the Parabolic SAR plots dots above or below price to represent trend direction and potential reversal points, often used as a trailing stop mechanism. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}
formula: For uptrend: SAR_t = SAR_{t-1} + AF × (EP − SAR_{t-1}); where AF is acceleration factor (starts 0.02, increments by 0.02 up to max 0.20), EP = extreme price (highest high in uptrend). Similar for downtrend. :contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}
parameters: Typical AF start = 0.02; AF step = 0.02; AF max = 0.20; timeframe adaptable (intraday to daily).

signal.buy: Dot moves below price after being above → trend reversal to bullish sign.
signal.sell: Dot moves above price after being below → trend reversal to bearish sign.
signal.neutral: Dots alternate frequently or move closely around price → market is choppy/sideways.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily), especially in trending markets for trailing stop / exit strategy.
strengths: Simple visual representation of trend and stop level; good tool for trailing exits and following momentum.
weaknesses: Poor performance in sideways/range markets—frequent false signals; less reliable when volatility is low. :contentReference[oaicite:11]{index=11}

name: Donchian Channel
description: An indicator developed by Richard Donchian that plots the highest high and lowest low over a specified period, forming a channel which helps identify breakout or trend-initiation points. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
formula: UpperBand = HighestHigh_n; LowerBand = LowestLow_n; Middle = (UpperBand + LowerBand) ÷ 2. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
parameters: Typical look-back period n = 20 (can adjust for timeframe/volatility).

signal.buy: Price breaks above UpperBand signalling a breakout/strong uptrend.
signal.sell: Price breaks below LowerBand signalling a breakout/strong downtrend.
signal.neutral: Price remains within the channel (UpperBand and LowerBand) indicating consolidation/no breakout.

best_timeframe: Short to medium-term (intraday to daily) especially effective in breakout/trend setups.
strengths: Simple and clear breakout zone; suitable for trend initiation and volatility expansion strategies.
weaknesses: Many false breakouts especially in choppy markets; gives little information on trend strength or exit timing.

name: Coppock Curve
description: An indicator created by E.S.C. Coppock originally for long-term stock market investing, but sometimes adapted for other markets. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
formula: Coppock = WMA[10] of (ROC[14] + ROC[11]) where ROC = rate of change. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}
parameters: Typical: ROC periods 14 & 11, WMA smoothing 10; mostly used on monthly charts originally.

signal.buy: Indicator bottoms and crosses above zero signalling early up-trend for long-term horizon.
signal.sell: Not primarily built for sell signals (original design), but some adapt by crosses below zero or other criteria.
signal.neutral: Indicator near zero and not showing clear upward momentum yet.

best_timeframe: Long term (monthly or multi-month) though can be adapted for shorter if parameters are changed.
strengths: Designed to capture major market bottoms/turns; less noise compared with short-term oscillators.
weaknesses: Very slow/lags substantially; not well-suited for short-term trading; less data support in non-stock-index markets.

name: Range Expansion Index (REI)
description: An indicator developed by Thomas R. DeMark that measures internal strength/weakness of price-range expansion and contraction to identify potential reversals. :contentReference[oaicite:9]{index=9}
formula: REI = (S1 ÷ S2) × 100 where S1 = sum of ‘strong’ price changes; S2 = sum of absolute price changes within look-back period n (commonly n = 8). :contentReference[oaicite:10]{index=10}
parameters: Typical look-back n = 8; thresholds around +60/-60 for signals.

signal.buy: REI falls below -60 and then rises above threshold signalling price strength emerging.
signal.sell: REI rises above +60 and then falls indicating weakness or potential reversal.
signal.neutral: REI between +60 and -60 without turning indicates no strong expansion or contraction yet.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term (intraday to daily) suitable for identifying reversal zones or exhaustion.
strengths: Helps detect range contraction/expansion dynamics; early signal of potential reversal of momentum.
weaknesses: Less commonly used (less widespread support); can give false signals in very volatile or trending markets without clear contraction phases.

name: Absolute Currency Strength (ACS)
description: An indicator that measures the absolute strength or weakness of a currency (or asset) relative to historical performance, often used in forex but illustrative for other assets. :contentReference[oaicite:12]{index=12}
formula: ACS = Percentage gain or loss of currency (or asset) over recent period (e.g., N periods) mapped relative to other instruments; formula varies by implementation. :contentReference[oaicite:13]{index=13}
parameters: Typical look-back period configurable (e.g., 15 or more); more effective in currency or correlated-asset strategies.

signal.buy: Asset shows strong ACS reading (relative strength high) while paired asset shows weakness → trade strong asset vs weak asset.
signal.sell: Asset shows weak ACS reading (relative strength low) while paired asset shows strength → considered for selling or shorting context.
signal.neutral: ACS is moderate / no clear strength vs weakness distinction.

best_timeframe: Short to medium term though often used in intraday/FX contexts for strength/weakness strategies rather than pure timing.
strengths: Highlights relative strength/weakness across assets or currencies; useful for pairs trading, spread trading or identifying strong vs weak assets.
weaknesses: Less conventional in commodity/trend trading compared to mainstream indicators; formula and thresholds more subjective; requires cross-asset data.

name: Haurlan Index
description: An indicator developed by P.N. ‘Pete’ Haurlan that uses multiple exponential moving averages of the accumulation/distribution line to gauge short, intermediate, and long-term market breadth and momentum. :contentReference[oaicite:16]{index=16}
formula: Three components: EMA_short, EMA_mid, EMA_long applied to A/D line; composite then interpreted relative to previous values. :contentReference[oaicite:17]{index=17}
parameters: Typically uses varying lengths for short, intermediate, and long EMAs (e.g., 20, 50, 200).

signal.buy: Composite component turns upward from trough and breadth confirms shift from accumulation to markup phase.
signal.sell: Composite turns downward indicating shift from markup to distribution phase.
signal.neutral: Values are flat or divergent without clear change in breadth phases.

best_timeframe: Medium to long term (daily to weekly) useful for macro/market-breadth insight rather than granular entry timing.
strengths: Provides broader market context; helps detect shift in market phase (accumulation/distribution) rather than individual asset signal.
weaknesses: Less useful for precise timing; lag significant; more complex to interpret and less commonly used than standard indicators.
